title.rendered: Jehovah Shalom, the Lord Is Peace: The Gospel For Today

content.rendered:
Gideon expected to die after seeing the Angel of the Lord face to face. Instead he built an altar and called it Jehovah Shalom, the Lord Is Peace.

The Gospel For Today | Saturday, August 15, 2026

Today’s Scripture

“So Gideon built an altar there to the LORD, and called it The-LORD-Is-Peace. To this day it is still in Ophrah of the Abiezrites.”
Judges 6:24 (NKJV)

Today’s Message

Gideon was threshing wheat in a winepress, hiding it from raiding Midianites, when the Angel of the Lord appeared and called him “mighty man of valour” — a title that did not yet match the fearful man crouched in a pit (Judges 6:11-12). When Gideon realised he had seen the Angel of the Lord face to face, his first reaction was not comfort. It was terror, because the ancient assumption was that no one could see God and live (Judges 6:22).

God’s response was immediate: “Peace be with you, do not fear; you shall not die” (Judges 6:23). And Gideon, still shaking, built an altar right there and named it Jehovah Shalom — not “the Lord gives peace” as a general truth, but “the Lord is peace,” as a description of His very nature at the exact moment Gideon expected judgment instead.

Shalom is a richer word than the English “peace” suggests. It carries wholeness, completeness, nothing broken and nothing lacking — not merely the absence of conflict but the presence of everything working as it should. The Message paraphrase captures the moment simply: “God said, ‘Easy. Don’t panic. You won’t die.’ Gideon built an altar to God and named it ‘God’s Peace.’” (Judges 6:23-24 MSG).

What makes this name significant is its timing. It was not spoken over a peaceful nation — Israel was under seven years of Midianite oppression, hiding grain in caves, terrified enough that an angel had to find Gideon threshing in secret. Jehovah Shalom was declared in the middle of the mess, not after it was cleaned up. Peace, in the biblical sense, is not the absence of a threatening situation. It is the presence of God in the middle of one.

If your circumstances look like Gideon’s — oppressed, hiding, more aware of the enemy’s size than your own — know that Jehovah Shalom does not wait for the Midianites to leave before He shows up. He shows up in the winepress, calls the fearful man valiant, and tells him not to panic, because peace is not a feeling you wait for. It is a Person you have already met.

Prayer

Father, You are Jehovah Shalom. In the middle of my mess, before my circumstances change, You are already my peace. Quiet the panic in me today. Where I feel more aware of the threat than of You, remind me that You are present, and where You are present, wholeness follows. In Jesus’ name. Amen.

Declaration

My God is Jehovah Shalom. He is my peace, not after my circumstances change, but right now, in the middle of them. I will not panic. I am not what I used to be; I am who He calls me.
